verses.1: And Hannah prayed, saying, “May the Lord grant me peace in this time of sorrow. May He open my mouth wide to speak to my enemies, for I have rejoiced in your salvation.”
verses.2: There is no god like Yahweh, for there is no one else besides Him. And no creature is equal to our God.
verses.3: Do not speak in a high voice. A great disaster will come from among you. For this is what the Lord knows; it has been planned for you.
verses.4: The gates of heaven are closed, and they fail; then the army is destroyed.
verses.5: Seventy people were sold as slaves; the hungry ones stopped eating altogether. She had seven children, and her husband became very old.
verses.6: YHWH kills and lives again; He removes Sheol from its place.
verses.7: Yehovah is the one who destroys and enriches those who are humble.
verses.8: It is built from stones that have been taken from the ruins of ancient buildings. It serves as a place for those who are generous and honorable to dwell in. For Jehovah has given them these lands, and He has covered them with dew.
verses.9: The feet of their righteous ones will be protected, while the wicked will be destroyed in darkness. It seems that no one can overcome them.
verses.10: May Jehovah divide his enemies from him in the heavens. May Jehovah strike down those who oppose him on earth. And may he give strength to his king. May he also raise up a pillar for his Messiah.
verses.11: And Elkanah the priest went to his house. The young man was the servant of Jehovah, and he served at the prophet’s house.
verses.12: And the sons of Eli, and the sons of Beliael, did not know Jehovah at all.
verses.13: And the priests judged the people. Every one who offered an offering, the priest brought it with him. The priest also carried three rods in his hands.
verses.14: And he shall strike it with a club, or with a rod, or with a staff, or with a pole. All those who come there shall be struck by it. The priest shall do this for all the Israelites who come there.
verses.15: Also, before they were able to separate the milk from it, the young priest came and said to the man who was milking the sheep, “Give some meat to the priest for his meals. Do not take any spoiled meat from you, except for those who are alive.”
verses.16: And the man said to him, “Kater will light the fire for them on that day when the milk is ready. But take it with you, as your soul desires. Do not give it now; otherwise, I won’t take it even if I try hard.”
verses.17: The sin of those young men was extremely serious; it brought shame upon the face of Jehovah. For the people took away Jehovah’s offerings.
verses.18: And Shemuel served before the face of Jehovah. He was a young man who wore a crown on his head.
verses.19: And a little offering will be made for him by his mother. She has prepared it since ancient times, when she offered her daughter as an offering to God.
verses.20: And He blessed Elkanah and his wife. Then He said, “May Jehovah give you a son from this woman, under the condition that she fulfill the vows she made to Jehovah.” And they went to that place.
verses.21: For Jehovah had appointed Canaan as a land of promise. It became fertile and gave birth to three sons and two daughters. And the young man named Shemuel was raised up by Jehovah.
verses.22: And when I reach old age, I will hear all that my sons do for all of Israel. And I will also hear about those who lay women who are not yet married in their tombs. Then I will open the door of the tomb.
verses.23: And he said to them, “Why do you do these things? I hear that your words are bad ones from all these people.”
verses.24: Do not say, “It is not good to hear what I hear from Jehovah’s people.”
verses.25: If one person sins against another, and God forgives them, then who will pray to Him? No one will listen to their prayers. For God wants to destroy them all.
verses.26: And the boy Shmuel grew up to be a good person, both with God and with people around him.
verses.27: And a man of God came to him and said, “As the Lord has said, ‘I have been revealed before your father’s house, while they were in Egypt, in Pharaoh’s house.’”
verses.28: And I have chosen him from all the tribes of Israel to be my priest, so that he may offer sacrifices on my altar. He will also carry the incense before me. And I will give to your house all the offerings from the children of Israel.
verses.29: Why do you waste my offerings and my sacrifices? I commanded them to be offered as offerings. You have spoiled your children by turning them away from me, so that they might not be born again from my hand. Every offering of Israel belongs to my people.
verses.30: Therefore, let the LORD, the God of Israel, say that I will make His house and the house of my father’s family walk before Me forever. Now, let the LORD say, “Be merciful to me, for I am humble and weak.”
verses.31: Now, days are coming, and I will see your descendants and the descendants of your father’s house. They will become old in your house.
verses.32: And you shall take away all the impurities from all those who have done wrong to Israel. No one should become old in your house forever.
verses.33: And no man will be able to stand before you in my temple, to deceive your eyes and to corrupt your heart. All those who are in your house will die.
verses.34: And this will happen to you as well: both of your sons will die on the same day.
verses.35: And I appointed for myself a faithful priest, who will do what is right in my heart and mind. I also built a house for him, so that he could serve before my Messiah all the days of his life.
verses.36: And all those who are sick in your house shall come to you to be healed with silver and bread. And he shall say, “Please take me to one of the priests so that I can eat some bread.”
